result.label: A01-blind-audit-core
result.summary: nfl-blind-audit.js is a sound, transactional week-chain controller for the 2021-25 HISTORICAL replay only: it freezes working-tree code (server/scripts/package*) and a season-scoped hash of 31 input tables at preregistration, re-verifies both before compute and again under BEGIN IMMEDIATE before sealing each week, and chains result hashes. It does not implement the 2026 forward "blind audit" its own protocol text names (startWeek floor 5, classification hard-coded, and a season<=2026 freeze would be voided by the live capture that inserts ~250k quote/line rows per day); the forward evidence lives in shadow_decisions/decision tape, which this file only reads in the look-back. nfl_blind_input_mutations is a table-name-only change detector (5.05M rows, no values, no pruning) that lets assertFrozen skip a full rehash; with live capture it never skips, so week opens pay up to 133 s of rehash. Bets are counted per market separately and merged; units come from nfl-replay picks; ROI divides by all bets including pushes; run 32's spread record (156 bets, 74-79-3, -11.088u) reproduces exactly from picks. Week-level cutoff enforcement is entirely delegated to nfl-replay/expert-council/ensemble; this layer passes only (season, week) against a whole-season snapshot. Main defects: the chain/result hash includes look-back diagnostics read from unfrozen tables (nfl_odds_archive, shadow_decisions), so compareAuditRuns conflates non-economic changes with forecast changes (C09); a per-market replay error is silently dropped from the week; auditOverview derives expected weeks from observed min/max so an early-stopped run reports complete coverage. audit-registry is a separate, narrow preregister/run-once registry with a services-only code hash and row-count data signature; not a leakage surface.

All week-level exclusion is delegated to nfl-replay.js (weekCutoffIso :539), weekly-backtest.js (no cutoff string at all), nfl-expert-council.js and nfl-ensemble.js; this layer cannot detect a week N+1 read inside them.

defects.claim: result_hash and chain_hash cover the look-back, which is built from unfrozen tables (nfl_odds_archive :673, shadow_decisions :758, nfl_nfelo_games, nfl_external_ratings), so two runs on identical frozen code and data can produce different hashes and compareAuditRuns will report a forecast/policy/data change (C09 conflation).
defects.impact: Reproducibility checks and run comparisons can flag non-economic diagnostic drift as a real model change; the chain hash no longer certifies the frozen forecast alone.
defects.fix: Hash forecast/picks/summary separately from diagnostics (lookback, reasoning) and have compareAuditRuns report artifact, forecast, selection and cash-flow deltas separately; or add the look-back tables to INPUT_TABLES.

defects.claim: A per-market replay error is filtered out silently; metrics.error is only set when every market fails, so a week with a spread-only failure is sealed with the market missing and no failure recorded.
defects.impact: A week can be sealed with a missing market and pass runManifest.failures (:545 checks only metrics.error) and auditOverview coverage; missing computation is indistinguishable from a healthy zero-bet week (C02 'represent unavailable computation explicitly').
defects.fix: Record each errored market in metrics (e.g. by_market[market] = { error }) and in runManifest.failures; treat it as an incomplete week in the overview.

defects.claim: The protocol text names this controller as the preregistered 2026 forward ledger, but no forward mode exists: startWeek is floored at 5 (:171), classification is fixed to historical replay (:176), and a seasons:[2026] run would freeze season<=2026 rows (:130, afterSeason 2027-03-01 :107-108) which live capture (250k quote/line inserts in the last 24h per the journal) voids at the next week open.
defects.snippet: 'development and cannot claim a newly discovered edge. The BLIND AUDIT is the preregistered 2026 forward ledger.',
defects.impact: Anyone following the protocol will believe the forward ledger is operated by this controller; it is not, and the actual 2026 evidence (shadow_decisions, decision tape) has no week-chain, freeze or manifest here.
defects.fix: Either implement a distinct forward mode (weekly cutoff freeze of only rows received before T-60, no season-wide rehash) or correct the protocol text to point at the decision tape / shadow ledger as the forward mechanism.

defects.claim: Expected weeks are derived from the observed min/max of present weeks rather than the run's declared spec_json.schedule, so a run that stopped early (e.g. run 28 at 22 of 70 weeks) reports every season complete and coverage_complete true.
defects.snippet:
for (let week = c.min_week; week <= c.max_week; week++) expected.push(week);
      const missing = expected.filter(week => !c.weeks.has(week));
defects.impact: C09 asks for exact expected/present/valid week sets; a truncated run is presented as complete coverage, and a season with no opened weeks at all is absent rather than listed as missing.
defects.fix: Parse spec_json.schedule for the declared (season, week) set and report declared/present/missing against it; also mark status != complete as incomplete coverage.

defects.claim: weekly_input is labelled as frozen before outcomes are read, but it copies combined_decision wholesale (:635) which contains settlement.directional_correct.
defects.impact: The stored 'pregame input' record contains graded outcome fields; a reader treating it as a pre-outcome artifact is misled.
defects.fix: Strip settlement fields from combined_decision in weeklyInput or rename the record as a graded projection.

defects.claim: uncertainty(bets) is run on one week's bets (a single week cluster), so the weekly-cluster bootstrap resamples one cluster 4000 times; seed and draw count are not saved with the result.
defects.snippet: uncertainty: uncertainty(bets),
defects.impact: Per-week intervals stored in every result_json are not meaningful, and C09's 'save bootstrap cohort, seed and draw count' is unmet.
defects.fix: Drop the per-week bootstrap or compute it only at aggregate level with the cohort, seed and draws recorded.

defects.claim: final.betting reports bets/wins/losses/units/roi but not pushes; run 32 final shows 550 bets, 207 wins, 339 losses and the 4 pushes must be inferred.
defects.snippet:
betting: { bets: totalBets, wins: bets.reduce((s, x) => s + x.wins, 0),
      losses: bets.reduce((s, x) => s + x.losses, 0), units: +units.toFixed(3),
defects.impact: Pushes are invisible in the sealed final record; consumers must subtract.
defects.fix: Add pushes: bets.reduce((s,x)=>s+(x.pushes??0),0).

defects.claim: spread_only treats a missing unit figure as 0 (units: pick.units ?? 0, summed at :196) while by_market explicitly counts missing_units and excludes them; the two blocks disagree on the same picks.
defects.snippet:
allBets.push({ season: w.season, week: w.week, market, result,
        units: pick.units ?? 0, units_known: pick.units != null });
defects.impact: spread_only.units/roi silently absorb unknown stakes as zero, the exact failure C09 names; ROI denominators in both blocks also include pushes, voids and unknown-unit picks.
defects.fix: Carry units_known into spread_only and report missing_units there; document the ROI denominator.

defects.claim: The Sidak-corrected alpha at run time uses the number of audits sealed so far, so earlier audits face a laxer threshold than auditHistory later reports for the same audit.
defects.snippet:
const priorTests = row(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM audit_registry WHERE status='sealed'`)?.n ?? 0;
  const correctedAlpha = 1 - Math.pow(1 - 0.05, 1 / Math.max(1, priorTests + 1));
defects.impact: Stored significant flag can disagree with auditHistory.survive_correction; run order changes pass/fail.
defects.fix: Store the alpha used, and let auditHistory recompute significance against the final count while showing both.

defects.claim: The mutation journal records only table_name/operation/changed_at (schema nfl-a-to-m.js:157-162), has 5,048,401 rows with no pruning, and with continuous live capture the fast path never fires: freeze_check_ms averaged 3.2 s (max 52.7 s) on run 27 and 7.7 s (max 133 s) on run 28.
defects.snippet: if (priorMutation >= 0 && mutations.latest <= priorMutation) return;
defects.impact: Every week open during live capture pays a full 31-table rehash; the journal grows unbounded. Operational cost, not a correctness hole (scoped rehash is still correct).
defects.fix: Journal table+scope key (season or commence_time bucket) so out-of-scope writes can be skipped, and prune rows older than the oldest open run's cursor.

defects.claim: The test imports server/db/index.js without setting GRIDIRON_DB_PATH, so it opens the live data.sqlite and depends on runs 27/31 existing (skips otherwise).
defects.snippet: const { row } = await import('../server/db/index.js');
defects.impact: C06 dependence on private history; the test touches the production DB file from the suite.
defects.fix: Move the run-27 reproduction to a data-validation suite and keep only synthetic cases in the required suite.

defects.claim: freeze_check_ms measures only the pre-compute assertFrozen; the second assertFrozen under the writer lock (:893) is counted in persist_ms.
defects.snippet: const freezeCheckMs = performance.now() - startedAt;
defects.impact: Timing-by-phase under-reports freeze cost and over-reports persist cost (run 32 persist avg 21.5 s is mostly the rehash).
defects.fix: Time the recheck separately or add it to freeze_check_ms.

point_in_time_guarantees: Code freeze: sha256 of every tracked+untracked file under server/, scripts/, package.json, package-lock.json in the working tree must equal runs.code_hash before every week open and again under the writer lock before sealing (nfl-blind-audit.js:74-93, :229-231, :848, :893); docs/client/tests excluded; commit id recorded but not hashed.

Data freeze: per-table sha256 over season-scoped rows (season<=maxSeason; time cutoffs < maxSeason+1-03-01; players and nfl_teams column-scoped) for all 31 INPUT_TABLES must equal runs.data_hash whenever the mutation journal has advanced (:96-158, :232-248); rehash is skipped only when no journal row landed since the cursor.

Atomic seal: week row, expert examples, postgame truth, run progress and timing are written in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction after a second assertFrozen; any throw rolls everything back and only a retry row survives (:890-917, :829-840).

Chronological chain: schedule is season-major weeks 5-18; ordinal N+1 cannot open before ordinal N; chain_hash = sha(prior_chain:ordinal:season:week:result_hash) (:160-164, :883-886); UNIQUE(run_id, season, week) in the table.
Persistent ensemble fits are neither read nor written during the audited week (withEphemeralEnsembleArtifacts, nfl-ensemble.js:951-962).
Coordinator and neural experts train only on rows persisted by the same run with (season<target OR (season=target AND week<target)) (nfl-expert-coordinator.js:258-260, nfl-expert-council.js:280-282).

NOT guaranteed here: any week-level exclusion of later rows inside the season snapshot (delegated to callees); freezing of nfl_odds_archive, nfl_nfelo_games, nfl_external_ratings, shadow_decisions, nfl_game_variance; an immutable pre-outcome packet per game (C11) — the controller stores computed outputs, not the input rows consumed.

result.label: A03-decision-tape-ledgers
result.summary: The decision tape (nfl_decision_runs/events, migrations 027+031) and the execution lifecycle ledger are close to the plan's §4.1/§7.3 contract as code: schema-level append-only triggers, separate observation vs content identity, atomic header+children, append-only invalidations and settlement corrections, and a CLV projection scoped to canonical event + full_game period + per-book latest quote with a declared book set. But (1) the live DB holds ZERO decision runs, zero opportunities, zero forward_picks and zero nfl_bet_log rows; the only 2026 forward evidence is shadow_decisions (189 rows, 14 settled) which is mutable (UPDATE on settle), trigger-less, unhashed, first-capture-wins, and grades CLV against the LIVE game_lines.spread rather than closing_spread. (2) The T-60 runner freezes a packet but never calls recordDecisionRun (decision_run_id stays NULL); every pipeline run hard-codes data_identity_status='unfrozen_live_tables', so no decision is reproducible from stored inputs — the status register is correct, and slightly generous, on this. (3) The tape has no clock guard (decidedAt is never compared with the caller-declared cutoffAt), and its content hash covers forecast outputs and identity ids but not the feature packet it persists. (4) CLV: no freshness bound on "latest per book" (a days-old quote still defines a book's close), price CLV is vigged and includes the bet-at book by default, and a legacy nfl_bet_log CLV with an incompatible single-instant definition is still scheduled. (5) Settlement corrections are append-only on the lifecycle ledger, but lifecycleFunnel and threeWayAttribution read only the original settled row, so a corrected result is invisible to them; forward_picks/shadow_decisions/nfl_bet_log grade exactly once via WHERE result IS NULL and have no correction path at all.

defects.claim: The only ledger holding 2026 forward evidence (189 rows, 14 settled in the live DB) is mutable: settlement UPDATEs the prediction row, the table has no append-only triggers, no content hash, and dedup is code-only first-capture-wins
defects.snippet: run(`UPDATE shadow_decisions SET settled_at=?,outcome_json=?,result=?,clv_points=? WHERE id=?`,
defects.impact: Every 2026 number Nick can currently cite comes from a table that can be rewritten silently and cannot be re-derived; none of the plan's §4.1 identity or §7.3 correction properties apply to it
defects.fix: Retire shadow-ledger writes in favour of recordDecisionRun with a declared observation, or add append-only settlement/correction rows and schema triggers plus a content hash

defects.claim: forward_picks settlement mutates the decision row (result, closing_line, clv_points, settled_at) with no trigger protection, contradicting the file's own 'cannot be retrofitted' claim

run(`UPDATE forward_picks SET closing_line = ?, actual_margin = ?, actual_total = ?,
         result = ?, clv_points = ?, settled_at = ? WHERE id = ?`,
defects.impact: Decision and settlement are one mutable record; a re-grade or manual edit is undetectable
defects.fix: Separate append-only settlement table keyed by pick id, triggers on forward_picks, correction events

defects.claim: No clock guard: decidedAt defaults to now and is never compared with the caller-declared cutoffAt or any kickoff; validateObservation only checks cutoffAt parses (:247)

defects.impact: A run recorded after kickoff with a declared past cutoff is indistinguishable in identity from a genuine T-60 observation, the exact failure the module header says it prevents

defects.claim: feature_snapshot is persisted in full but excluded from the content hash (fingerprint :104-171 hashes outputs and identity ids only); differing inputs with identical outputs share a content address and a same-observation retry drops the differing snapshot as created:false

defects.claim: Every decision run hard-codes unfrozen_live_tables and the T-60 runner (t60-runner.js:127,292) never calls recordDecisionRun; live DB has 0 decision runs and the one frozen packet has decision_run_id NULL
defects.snippet: dataIdentityStatus: 'unfrozen_live_tables',
defects.impact: No decision is reproducible from stored inputs and no prospective decision has been recorded at all; the tape is disconnected from the only prospective capture path

defects.claim: 'Latest quote per book' has no freshness bound; the only time filter is snapshot_at < kickoff (:129) with an 8h commence_time window (:131), so a book's days-old last quote defines its close and enters the main-line mode (:160) and price average (:174)
defects.snippet: if (!held || q.snapshot_at > held.snapshot_at) latestPerBook.set(q.bookmaker_key, q);
defects.impact: Closing benchmark can be built from stale books; C13 named freshness explicitly and the test file has no stale-close case
defects.fix: Declare a maximum age before kickoff per contributing book, exclude and report stale books separately

defects.claim: Price CLV is computed in vigged implied-probability space against an average of every book including the one bet at; no de-vig from paired quotes and no independent reference set (declared_books defaults to all)
defects.snippet: const closeImplied = impliedProbability(close.price);
defects.impact: clv_probability measures 'our book vs average vigged book', which is not the same-line fair-price CLV C14 asks for and is biased toward zero by including the target book
defects.fix: Pair each book's quote with its mirror contract, de-vig (Shin), average fair probabilities, and default the reference set to exclude the accepted book

defects.claim: lifecycleFunnel joins only state='settled' rows for wins/losses (:473) and realized_pnl_units (:476), ignoring settlement_correction events

result.label: A05-replay-engines
result.summary: THE historical audit is blind-audit runs 27/31/32 (nfl_blind_audit_runs), whose betting kernel is nfl-replay.js#replaySeason; every other engine here is a duplicate or a research-only wrapper. Critical finding: the production board fixes blendMode 'market_residual' (nfl-auto-picks.js:83) but replaySeason, the blind audit, the family report, the AI replay and cover calibration all call ensembleLine with the default 'raw' blend, so the entire 2021-25 spread record grades a graph that is not served (the family evidence JSON's baseline MAE 10.095 vs market 9.762 is impossible for the residual graph). Ensemble weights/residual slopes are genuinely walk-forward per (season, week) via fitEnsemble cutoffs (847 persisted artifacts, 183 cutoffs), but feature calibration is one static fit on <2022. All historical engines grade at the close with prices; opener exposure is disclosed as non-executable diagnostics; only line-move-study/beat-the-close price the opener. C16 (family ablation): scoring math is fixed, but 'refit_leave_one_family_out' is false — fitEnsemble has no families parameter, ensembleLine filters MODELS after fitting and renormalises frozen weights; cost is inferred; consumer check ignores fitted weight (Context family delta exactly 0). Seven parallel bet-select-grade engines and four bootstrap implementations exist. Beat-the-close (the only forward engine) has an unwired retirement loop (nfl_rule_state empty), an opener baseline that falls back to first live capture, and two live rules Phase 1 never passed. line-move-study leaks actual kickoff weather into T2 features and selects ratings hyperparameters without a selectionThrough on the served report. Persisted runs: nfl_replay_runs 0, nfl_neural_replay_audits 0, nfl_ai_replay_runs 0, nfl_policy_audits 1 (Aug 24), family evidence JSON one run; preregistered scripts sealed as negative results (#13 0.438, #15 0.483).

result.label: A04-packet-quotes-time
result.summary: The T-60 clock taxonomy (effective/published/received, kickoff-60 cutoff, response-completion receipt gate, canonical-event + market/period predicate) is correctly implemented and tested in nfl-t60-packet.js, but it is dead in production: all 1,321 quote batches in the live DB (including all 1,153 book_feeds batches captured 2026-09-02..12) carry receipt_clock_source='legacy_request_time_only' because book-feeds.js:417 and line-shopping.js:66 never pass receivedAt, so the packet's only prospective-capable source can never reach received_by_cutoff and the single frozen observation (SF@LAR 2026-09-10) holds no eligible price. The durable runner stores only a non-canonical sha256 of JSON.stringify(packet) that embeds a wall clock and discards the packet content (no payload column in migration 034), and the section-4.1 forecast-packet contract has no producer or consumer. Five of six packet sources are still counts, news is unscoped (global), and 'missed' is unreachable through runT60Pass because capture runs before mark-missed with no upper bound. Historical tape timestamps are honest but not decision-time: nfl_quote_tape 2020-25 rows are the-odds-api historical snapshots (1-4 per event, 91% >24h pre-kickoff, received 2026-09-09) and the OddsTrader archive is open+last-pre-kickoff pairs only (14% of 'close' rows stamped after commence_time), fetched 2026-09-02. The 2021-25 replay (nfl-replay.js:193/203) and ensemble market anchor (nfl-ensemble.js:1317) use game_lines.spread = nflverse closing consensus as the market line, disclosed in-file as a number unobtainable at decision time; the settled -2.28 CLV was therefore measured beat-the-close with closing-time features, not at T-60.

result.label: A02-diagnostics-findings
result.summary: Statistical primitives are correct at the line (Holm step-down verified numerically; percentile/cluster paired bootstrap; mSPRT closed form matches Johari-Pekelis-Walsh; C17 relabel honest at the source). The candidate-findings ledger cannot promote through its API without three holdout passes, but: (1) the ONLY live finding (id 1, spread_x_timing, discovered 2026-09-09) is already stale — its stored rule hash (old git scheme) != the current 186-file code-identity closure I recomputed — and at 2026 season end recordHoldoutTest throws OUTSIDE its try (line 209), the orchestrator loop has no per-finding isolation, and nfl-model-growth's catch marks the whole season-end run 'error' and rethrows, aborting neural/risk-lab/player/expert settlement; segment_key UNIQUE means the finding can never be renewed (C08 not closed). (2) Holdout 'confirmation' is helped_holdout = ROI-after > ROI-before on one season — a directional coin flip with no effect size, interval, or minimum n; P(3 false passes | null) ~12.5%. (3) Development seasons 2021-2025 are not fenced as holdout for algorithmic findings; POST /profitability/model-growth/run accepts body.season. (4) Promotion trusts a mutable state column; tests reach promotion by SQL UPDATE; the real holdout path is untested. (5) audit-registry collapses p_always_valid ?? p_fixed_sample_only and gates on it against the Sidak alpha — the C17 relabel is neutralized at its only gating consumer, though no audit has ever supplied a sequence (always_valid_p NULL on all 15 rows) and decay-watch runs are all insufficient_data. (6) pairedBootstrapDiff silently falls back to the under-covering ungrouped resample when groups.length < n. (7) nfl-candidate-analysis macroDiagnosis ships hard-coded verdicts ('The candidate is not profitable', 'regime_instability: critical') as computed diagnosis. Diagnostics (slice, abstention, specialist, passing, coordination, nflDiagnostic) are descriptive and mostly labelled honestly; minor label/threshold issues only.

result.label: A05-replay-engines
result.summary: One historical spread engine (replaySeason in nfl-replay.js) sits under ~8 wrappers including the sealed blind audit (runs 27/32) that the plan treats as THE historical audit and then demotes to development data; the T-60 prospective ledger is the audit going forward and none of these engines consumes the frozen packet. Fits are walk-forward per cutoff (fitEnsemble beforeSeason/beforeWeek, cached artifacts), but every replay - blind audit included - runs the ensemble with blendMode 'raw' while the served board uses 'market_residual' (nfl-auto-picks.js:83), so runs 27/32 audit a different forecast than production. Opener vs close is disclosed honestly in nfl-replay (two labeled non-executable diagnostics), line-move-study and beat-the-close; neural replay, walkforward, football-first and trend-totals grade at the close (neural silently). Five independent research replays duplicate the question (neural prequential, weekly ridge walk-forward, per-season football-first, line-move logit, live beat-the-close shadow); family ablation exists twice (nfl-family-contribution vs nfl-research), both labeled 'refit_leave_one_family_out' although families only filter MODELS in ensembleLine and never reach fitEnsemble (frozen-fit renormalization). C16 scoring fixes (challenger_only propagation, conditional/three-state Brier) are real and test-pinned; refit-vs-removal, model-count-as-cost, missing graph/fit identities remain open. Line-move-study's passed signals rest on a T2 feature that is actual kickoff-hour weather, ratings hyperparameters selected through 2024 by default (inside the 2024-25 holdout), and nfelo backfilled lines of unverified historical availability. Beat-the-close runs two rules the study did not pass and uses first-live-capture as 'opener'. Execution replay is pure, deterministic and well-tested. Live DB: 0 nfl_replay_runs, 0 neural/AI runs, 847 fit artifacts, 61 frozen / 6 settled beat-the-close shadow decisions.

result.label: A03-decision-tape-ledgers
result.summary: The append-only decision tape (nfl-decision-tape.js + migrations 027/031) is well built: content hash covers board, policy, horizon/cutoff, real code-closure hash and data-identity status; observation key is separate; writes are atomic; UPDATE/DELETE triggers exist; every C01/C02 close-with clause has a passing test. The lifecycle ledger (023/028, nfl-execution-lifecycle.js) separates settlement from decision, records a finality basis, and corrects via appended deltas. nfl-execution-clv.js grades accepted tickets against a declared book set, full_game period, per-book latest pre-kickoff quote, with quote IDs and a grading version. BUT on the live DB (2026-09-11) the tape, lifecycle ledger, forward_picks and nfl_bet_log all have 0 rows: Week 1 decisions were written by the scheduler's nfl_decision_ledger job to the mutable nfl_pick_decisions UPSERT (16 rows), and the T-60 runner froze one packet (SF@LAR) but never calls the tape; the only tape caller is the manual pipeline route, which labels itself unscheduled. Reproducibility is honestly NO: the pipeline hard-codes data_identity_status='unfrozen_live_tables', data_hash is NULL, the tape stores forecast outputs not inputs, and schedule_version is never passed. The one ledger with 2026 rows, shadow_decisions, has the weakest guarantees: no kickoff guard (two SEA-NE rows captured 23h after kickoff and settled), close taken from the live game_lines.spread column that ESPN can overwrite in-game, in-place UPDATE settlement, no triggers. Corrections exist in the lifecycle ledger but lifecycleFunnel and threeWayAttribution still read the uncorrected settled row; the CLV report is never persisted so there is no grading-version artifact; 027 down() drops the tape tables.

result.label: A01-blind-audit-core
result.summary: The blind-audit controller (server/services/nfl-blind-audit.js) is a chronologically honest, hash-chained historical replay: every fit, coordinator training set and neural residual read is cut at (season<S OR week<W) and scoped to the run's own audit_run_id; the freeze (code hash over server/scripts/package*, per-table sha256 of 31 input tables, mutation-journal cursor) is checked before compute and again inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE before sealing. Runs 27/31/32 reproduce byte-identically over 70 weeks. However: (1) there is NO 2026 forward run anywhere in nfl_blind_audit_runs (all 24 runs are 2021-25/2022-25, weeks 5-18); the "blind forward ledger" the protocol text promises is not produced by this code. (2) Freeze scope is inverted in two places: the look-back reads four unfrozen tables (nfl_odds_archive, nfl_nfelo_games, nfl_external_ratings, shadow_decisions) whose values enter result_hash/chain_hash, while nfl_ensemble_fit_artifacts is hashed all_rows although the audit neither reads nor writes it, so a live server fit voids a run with no recovery (run 21 died exactly this way; run 28 on nfl_teams). (3) weekly_input is a projection of in-memory council output, not a persisted exact input packet (C11 not met here). (4) nfl_blind_input_mutations (5.06M rows) records only table/op/time, never a row; 3.3M of it is live quote/line-snapshot inserts, so the fast path never fires and every open does a full rehash (cheap: ~1.3s vs ~150s compute). (5) The C09 overview still miscounts: it lower-cases results then hands them to uncertainty() which matches 'Won'/'Lost', so spread_only.uncertainty.win_rate_95 is always [0,0] and the small-sample warning always fires; coverage completeness is derived from the observed min-max span not the run's declared schedule, so a run that died mid-season reports complete:true; missing units become 0 in spread_only and the bootstrap; roi divides known units by a denominator that includes missing-unit/void picks. (6) test/nfl-audit-overview.test.js opens the developer's live WAL database as a writer without GRIDIRON_DB_PATH and hard-codes run 27/31 figures - the C06 defect verbatim. Units: push 0, loss -1, win price/100 or 100/|price| at the stored historical (closing) price; roi = units/bets with pushes in the denominator; "void" exists only in the overview vocabulary, never in the replay; "fault" is a descriptive top-10 miss log that nothing reads back. result.verdict: Gridiron has two audit systems and neither produces admissible betting evidence today. The historical blind audit (runs 27/31/32) is chronologically honest and byte-reproducible but audits blendMode 'raw' (nfl-replay.js:225 -> nfl-ensemble.js:1221) while the board serves 'market_residual' (nfl-auto-picks.js:83), grades at the nflverse closing consensus with closing-time features (nfl-replay.js:193/203), and is development data by the plan's own section 9.2; the -7% ROI and -2.28 CLV are beat-the-close diagnostics of a non-served forecast. The forward 2026 lane is a set of well-tested modules that are not wired together in production: all 1,323/1,323 live quote batches carry the legacy request clock (book-feeds.js:417, line-shopping.js:66, nfl-quote-tape.js:64-65) so the T-60 packet can never admit a price (nfl-t60-packet.js:214); the runner stores a non-canonical hash and discards the packet (t60-runner.js:127-142, migration 034 has no payload column); Week 1 decisions went to the mutable nfl_pick_decisions UPSERT (scheduler.js:697-703) and the append-only tape has 0 rows; the only ledger with 2026 rows (shadow_decisions) captured two finished games 23h after the final with no kickoff guard (shadow-ledger.js:28-31); CLV is recomputed on every read and never persisted with the execution book inside the default reference (nfl-execution-clv.js:232, :59); and the single candidate finding is stale and will throw outside its try at nfl-candidate-findings.js:209, aborting the 2026 season-end learning cycle (nfl-model-growth.js:302-307). As of 2026-09-11 the number of admissible 2026 forward observations is zero. Even fully wired, a 272-game season with <=5 selections/week cannot decide ROI (n needed ~560 bets for +10%, ~2,250 for +5%); it can decide all-game T-60 CLV direction (~50-280 games depending on the effect) and prove pipeline integrity. Build order: receipt clock, persisted canonical packet, runner-to-tape decisions, shadow guard, persisted CLV grades, findings isolation, one clustered bootstrap over declared weeks, trial register with PBO/DSR haircut, pre-declared endpoints, then historical graph parity and relabel.

target_flow: SOURCES: every fact carries three clocks (effective_at, published_at, received_at); a decision may use only what was received before its cutoff; a request timestamp is never a receipt.
TAPE: append-only quote/injury/news/weather rows, never updated; corrections are new rows; the tape is the only input CLV may read.

PACKET: at the declared cutoff (kickoff-60) freeze the exact scoped rows (values, not counts) per game, hash them canonically with no wall clocks inside, persist the payload, and validate against one schema; a hash without content reconstructs nothing.

FORECAST: a pure function of (packet, fit artifact) whose fit cutoff precedes the packet cutoff; replay and served board call the identical function with identical, recorded options (blendMode is part of identity, never a default).

DECISION: one immutable tape run per (observation, game) in state selected/abstain/missed/unavailable; content hash over board+policy, observation key over when/why, data_hash = packet hash; the denominator is the declared schedule, not the rows that happened to be written.

SETTLEMENT: a separate appended event with a finality basis and declared score source; corrections are appended deltas; every report reads net units after corrections; nothing on the decision row changes.

CLV: one persisted grade per (decision, grading_version): declared reference book set excluding the execution book, period pinned to full_game, per-book latest quote received before kickoff, point CLV and price CLV in probability space with quote IDs and missing-close rate; new evidence appends a new grading version; CLV is supporting evidence, not profit.

REGISTER / FINDINGS: every attempted model, threshold, segment, family ablation and signal rule is registered before it is scored; discovery on development data (2021-25), confirmation only on data that did not exist when the rule was written (2026+), with a declared effect size, a weekly-clustered interval retaining zero-bet weeks, and a minimum matching count; multiplicity charged (Holm within a family, PBO/deflated Sharpe across the search).

GATE / VETO: promotion recounts evidence rows, requires a human actor and an append-only lifecycle; provenance is a narrow versioned manifest, a stale rule is isolated and recorded, and renewal starts a new version with zero evidence; a stale rule never vetoes and never crashes unrelated work.

INFERENCE: pre-declared fixed review endpoints (Week 9 integrity-only, Week 18 CLV); sequential tests only with sigma/tau declared from development data before the season and alpha-spending written in the register; ROI is not a 2026 endpoint because <=90 selections cannot resolve it.

HISTORICAL REPLAY: labelled development; one engine, same graph as served, as-of (bitemporal) inputs where they exist and disclosed closing-line basis where they do not; used to prove algorithmic chronology and develop candidates, never to grant betting authority.

verdicts.reasoning: Standard survives: a backtest/decision record must use point-in-time inputs stamped with when the system actually held them (bitemporal as-of receipt), not when it asked — and requestedAt<=receivedAt biases only toward admitting evidence too early. Code confirms the chain: nfl-quote-tape.js:61-66 defaults clockSource to 'legacy_request_time_only' when receivedAt is absent; book-feeds.js:417 `ingestQuoteSnapshot(payload, { provider:'free-book-feeds', requestedAt: at, ... })` and line-shopping.js:66 `ingestQuoteSnapshot(data, { requestedAt: at, markets, sourceRef:'snapshot_lines' })` both omit receivedAt; nfl-t60-packet.js:214-216 `realClock = scopedQuotes.filter(q => q.receipt_clock_source === 'response_completion')` then `receivedByCutoff = realClock.filter(...)`. Live DB: nfl_quote_batches GROUP BY receipt_clock_source returns a single row, legacy_request_time_only = 1342 (free-book-feeds 1174, latest 2026-09-12T07:44Z). The one frozen observation (nfl_t60_observations SF@LAR, cutoff 2026-09-10T23:35Z) sees 18,810 spread rows in its kickoff window, all legacy, so its quote entry can only be missing/quarantined. Only correction: nfl-quote-tape.js:127-137 and :164 do pass receiptClockSource 'response_completion', so the capability exists — it is the producers that actually run which are incapable. Applies fine at NFL sizes (a receipt timestamp costs one Date.now() per batch).

Standard survives and is the repo's own declared contract, not an outside opinion: forecast-packet.js:167-216 already states that a content address must be canonical (recursive key sort) and must exclude non-content fields ('hashing the attempt number would make every retry a different packet'). The runner violates both: t60-runner.js:141-143 `packetHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(packet))` — insertion-ordered — over a packet that carries `computation_started_at` (nfl-t60-packet.js:332), fed the wall clock at t60-runner.js:108, so two captures of byte-identical evidence address differently. t60-runner.js:127-129 stores only packet_hash, and migration 034_t60_runner_ledger.js:33-58 defines nfl_t60_observations with no payload column, so the content the hash addresses is unrecoverable; runT60Pass (t60-runner.js:249-258) returns counts and drops captured[].packet. The section 4.1 module is unwired: grep shows forecast-packet.js is imported only by test/forecast-packet-contract.test.js:20 — no producer, no consumer. A hash with no retained payload cannot reconstruct a decision; this is reproducibility, not taste.
